sources.title: Neblio MM2 Trading
observations: Public page exposes Calculator, Values, Servers, Discord, Value Changes, Offers, Search, and Filters.
Page displayed 'Matching Offers 3,138 Results' and live offer cards with usernames, timestamps, offered totals, item counts, and trade controls.
A public 'Submit Completed' control was observed.
The page explains that accepted Neblio trades are followed by an in-game trade, but the captured evidence does not show an individual completed-trade record or exit proof.
sources.evidence_type: Public offer feed and platform-method description
sources.proof_limit: Displayed offers are not independently verified completed trades.

sources.title: Traderie MM2 marketplace
observations: Public navigation exposes marketplace listings, value list, guides, FAQ, safe-trading guide, review standards, and product categories.
A public listing showed 1 x Raygun Gun 2025 requested in exchange for either 1 x Chroma Mortal Knife 2026 or 1 x Chroma Immortal Gun 2026, listed 9 hours earlier.
The listing showed seller rating 5.00 and 13 reviews, but required sign-up to view contact details and make offers.
sources.evidence_type: Public listing and platform aggregate claim
sources.proof_limit: The listing is a posted ask, not proof that the trade occurred; the aggregate successful-trade number was not supported by an inspectable individual transaction in the captured material.

sources.title: Traderie Review Standards
observations: Traderie permits reviews for completed trades and for a seller or buyer canceling after acceptance.
It prohibits reviews based on fabricated or mostly incorrect information and prohibits reviews for merely commenting on listings or pricing.
sources.proof_limit: A permitted review is not independently observable transaction proof, and no individual review passage or matching item/quantity pair was captured.

sources.title: MM2 Trade Hub Trade Feed
observations: The site describes its feed as live community trade posts, with item sides, total MM2 trade values, and messaging.
It explicitly says users post trades and use DMs to agree and close.
Its explanatory text states that trade counts are based on posted offers, not completed trades.
sources.evidence_type: Public trade-feed description and editorial disclosure
sources.proof_limit: The feed is offer evidence, not completed-trade evidence. No individual completed example with exact exit proof was captured.

sources.title: MM2 Trade Hub Editorial Policy
observations: The page says values are published by MM2Values.com and Supreme Values and that the site reads both lists several times daily.
It says some item values are estimated and that some items have no agreed value.
It states that the site's own trade counts come from player-posted trades and are not completed trades.
sources.proof_limit: This supports source provenance and the distinction between asks and completions, but does not establish realized prices.

sources.title: Traderie Safe Trading Guide
observations: A public safe-trading-guide page was accessible and exposed navigation to related support pages.
sources.proof_limit: The captured page contained no detailed, item-specific completion evidence.

conclusions: The completed evidence is insufficient to claim any individual MM2 trade with exact variants, quantities, and independently observable completion or exit proof.
Neblio exposes completed-trade submission/navigation, but the captured public record did not provide inspectable proof for a specific completion.
Traderie reviews and its headline successful-trade count may indicate platform activity, but the captured material does not tie them to a specific item pair, quantity, date, and realized exit.
MM2 Trade Hub explicitly distinguishes posted offers from completed trades; its trade feed should therefore be treated as ask/intent evidence.
No supported acceptance or profit probabilities can be derived from the captured evidence.

For a trader requiring a strict Supreme +15 floor and four-copy constraint, the evidence supports using public feeds only to identify candidate asks and platform mechanics. Any concession should be justified by an independently verified completed transaction or a documented, repeatable exit—not by a listing, value-list number, review count, or platform aggregate.
The captured material does not establish whether compact upgrades outperform liquid denominations, whether popular items outperform base values, or a quantitative concession threshold.
access_failures: No individual public completed-trade record with full exact item variants and quantities was captured.
No observable in-game completion, acceptance event, or subsequent resale/exit was captured.
Traderie required sign-up to view contact details and make offers on the inspected listing.
Public platform claims and review systems were not sufficient to verify a specific completed trade.
